Thanks, Priyom — I reviewed Streamline's redline and annotate a few legal points below. My comments are inline in the attached Streamline_MSA-amendment-draft.pdf and consolidated-redline.xlsx. Key items: 

1) SLA credits: we can keep a credit schedule but need to limit cumulative credits to a 6-month lookback (protects against unlimited liability). Suggested clause: "cumulative SLA credits shall not exceed fees paid in any six (6) month period."

2) 60-day downshift notice: acceptable, but we need a mutuality clause that Redwood can request a temporary capacity hold for maintenance with 72 hours notice for emergency updates.

3) Data residency: confirmed — our private deployments in us-west-2 are supported but must be captured in order form with the region code. Stephanie, please confirm infra constraints.

4) Term/renewal cycles: Streamline's redline shortens automatic renewal to 30 days; we prefer 60 days for renewals with material capacity changes.

I recommend we consolidate into one redline that accepts Streamline's uplift and residency request, accepts a modified SLA credit cap, and preserves a 60-day renewal notice. I flagged exact language in the attached PDF.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Streamline_MSA-amendment-draft.pdf (pdf, 72KB); consolidated-redline.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)

Priyom / Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

• SLA credits cap: Streamline is ok with a cap BUT only if there is a remediation path (e.g., priority engineering review / dedicated support hours) included in the amendment. We don’t want an automated credit to be the only remedy.
• Renewal notice: we can accept 60 days for material changes, but we need assurance that renewal pricing for an uplift is priced pro-rata from the effective date.

Happy to take your suggested language on SLA cap + remediation. On the start date: we need the uplift to be effective June 1 given customer commitments; is that feasible operationally?

Evan Torres
